Warning, it's pretty heady, and even the elevator music might not be able to soothe your brain enough. You'll be forgiven if you skip to the 17 minute point where we'll turn it on, but then you'll have missed on the incredible physics miracle that happens inside.
cues.zh: 其实我记得很清楚，离真相也不远。这东西简直就是一个装在盒子里的完整量子物理实验室，这也引出了我们对铯原子钟工作原理的宏大解释。警告一下，这部分相当烧脑，甚至连电梯音乐可能都无法好好抚平你的大脑。如果你直接跳到 17 分钟处我们开机的地方，大家也是可以原谅的，但那样你就会错过内部发生的那场不可思议的物理奇迹。

cues.en: Let's start with cesium. It's a metal, quite heavy, that looks like gold and has a very low melting point at 28C, just above room temperature. If you could hold it, it would melt in your hands. But you can't hold it. It is the most reactive of all alkali metals, which are all pretty nasty. It will burn in air and explode in contact with water. Here's a video from Cody's lab showing what happens with a tiny drop.
cues.zh: 我们先从铯开始说起。它是一种很重的金属，看起来像黄金，熔点非常低，只有 28 摄氏度，刚过室温。如果你能拿着它，它会在你手中融化。但你拿不了。它是所有碱金属中最具反应性的，而碱金属本来就挺危险的。它会在空气中燃烧，接触水就会爆炸。这里是科迪实验室（Cody's lab）的一段视频，展示了一小滴会发生什么。

cues.en: Our clock has 7 grams in it, which would be enough to make quite an explosion. An alkali metal is one that comes from the first column of the periodic table of elements, like lithium or potassium. Caesium is the heaviest, so it's all the way at the bottom. Column 1 means it has only one valence electron on its outer electron shell, and that's the very one we are going to tackle in our atomic clock.
cues.zh: 我们的时钟里有 7 克铯，这足以引发一场大爆炸。碱金属是指来自元素周期表第一列的金属，比如锂或钾。铯是最重的，所以它在最底部。第一列意味着它的外层电子壳层只有一个价电子，而这正是我们要在原子钟里对付的家伙。

cues.en: But before we get there, we need to take a detour through spectroscopy and quantum mechanics. Scientists in the 19th century discovered that if you look at the flame of a burning element through a spectrophotometer like this one, which spreads the light in a rainbow like a prism would do, you get sharp lines in the spectrum, which are different for each element. Astronomers routinely use this to find out what distant stars are made of.
cues.zh: 但在我们讲到那里之前，我们需要绕道了解一下光谱学和量子力学。19世纪的科学家们发现，如果你通过像这样的分光光度计（它能像棱镜一样把光展开成彩虹）去观察燃烧元素的火焰，就会得到光谱中的尖锐线条，每种元素都不一样。天文学家经常用这个方法来探究遥远恒星的成分。

cues.en: And that's how Cesium was first discovered. It had two very characteristic blue lines, which color in Latin gave the element its name. It took the better part of a century to unravel the mystery of the spectral lines, which eventually led to the discovery of quantum mechanics. It turns out that our mysterious lines are due to our hot outer electron jumping through energy states that are not continuous, but confined to quantified levels.
cues.zh: Cesium就是这样被首次发现的。它有两条非常特征性的蓝线，拉丁语中的颜色赋予了该元素名称。揭开这些谱线之谜花了将近一个世纪，最终引出了量子力学的发现。原来，这些神秘谱线源于炽热的外层电子在能态间跃迁，而这些能态并非连续的，而是被限制在量子化能级上。

cues.en: When the jump occurs, the electron gives off a photon which color depends on the size of the energy step. The higher the step, the bluer the light. As the groundwork of quantum theory was being laid down, people were soon able to explain the core structure of the line with good approximation. But they were still puzzled by the finer details. If you look closer, you can observe that many of these lines come in pairs.
cues.zh: 跃迁发生时，电子释放出一个光子，其颜色取决于能量步长的大小。步长越大，光越蓝。随着量子理论基础的奠定，人们很快就能较好地近似解释谱线的核心结构。但他们仍对更精细的细节感到困惑。仔细观察，你会发现许多谱线是成对出现的。

cues.en: particularly visible in the sodium lines. This is called the fine structure. This riddle was solved by the discovery of the electron spin. As the electron rotates around the nucleus, it has quantized orbital momentum given the broad structure. But it also spins on itself like a planet and has its own spin momentum. It turns out the electron spin is also quantized and even more really
cues.zh: 这在钠谱线中尤为明显。这被称为精细结构。这个谜题通过电子自旋的发现得以解决。当电子绕原子核旋转时，它具有量子化的轨道角动量，从而形成宽泛的结构。但它也像行星一样自旋，拥有自己的自旋角动量。事实证明，电子自旋也是量子化的，而且更加——

cues.en: Only two values are allowed. These two values create two slightly different total energy levels within a single orbital quantum step, hence the line splitting. Now let's go back to our cesium spectra. Now that you have learned about a century of physics in five minutes, you can clearly recognize the split blue pair. But the doublet we are interested in is at the other end of the spectrum, actually in the near infrared.
cues.zh: 只允许两个值。这两个值在单一轨道量子步内产生两个略有不同的总能量级，因此导致谱线分裂。现在让我们回到铯的光谱。既然你已经在五分钟内学完了一个世纪的物理学，你就能清楚地辨认出分裂的蓝色双线。但我们感兴趣的双线位于光谱的另一端，实际上在近红外区域。

cues.en: It's called a D line, split into D1 and D2 by the electron spin. But if your head is not hurting yet, it's going to pretty soon, because it does not stop here. If you were to magnify this, you would see that each of the doublet lines is split even further. This is behind fine, and it is called the hyperfine structure. Here is the D2 line hyperfine structure in all of its glory.
cues.zh: 它被称为 D 线，被电子自旋分裂成 D1 和 D2。但如果你还没觉得头疼，那很快就会了，因为还没完。如果你把这个放大，你会发现每条双重线还会进一步分裂。这就是精细结构的背后原理，被称为超精细结构。这就是 D2 线超精细结构的完整面貌。

cues.en: this time in the form of an energy diagram. As we have seen, the D2 line transition, the big energy jump shown on the left, is at 852 nm in the infrared. We are finally getting there. Our super stable second is hidden in the splitting of the ground state at the bottom. The split is now caused by a quantized electromagnetic interaction between the spin of the electron and the spin of the nucleus.
cues.zh: 这次是以能级图的形式呈现。正如我们所见，左侧显示的 D2 线跃迁（那个巨大的能量跃迁）位于 852 纳米的红外波段。我们终于快接近核心了。我们超级稳定的“秒”就藏在底部基态的分裂之中。这种分裂是由电子自旋与原子核自旋之间量子化的电磁相互作用引起的。

cues.en: Note that this part of the picture is not to scale, the splits are now minuscule. So small in fact, that they are not in the visible spectrum anymore, but in the microwave spectrum. Do you see your second yet? See where it says 9.192631770 GHz. Exact. Yes my friend, this is what it is by definition. Not a fraction less or more of a hertz.
cues.zh: 注意，图中这部分并非按比例绘制，现在这些分裂微乎其微。实际上小到它们已经不在可见光光谱内，而是在微波光谱中。你看到你的“秒”了吗？看标有 9.192631770 GHz 的地方。分秒不差。是的，我的朋友，根据定义，它就是这个数值。一赫兹不多，一赫兹不少。

cues.en: You don't measure the atom with your instrument. The atom measures your instrument. It's just like what they say of our Soyuz clock. In Russia, you don't measure atom. Atom measures you. Okay, I see a microwave guide right here.
cues.zh: 不是你用仪器去测量原子。而是原子来测量你的仪器。就像他们对我们的联盟号时钟的评价一样。在俄罗斯，不是你测量原子。是原子测量你。好吧，我这里正好看到一个微波导轨。

cues.en: Okay, now that we know that our second comes from measuring the frequency of the hyperfine transition of the D2-line ground state of a neutral cesium atom at rest, all we need to do is to build a contraption to measure it. Piece of cake! The cesium tube is the heart of the instrument, so let's first look at what's inside. So this is pretty much a generic view of what a classic cesium beam tube looks like.
cues.zh: 既然我们知道了“秒”是由静止的中性铯原子基态 D2 线超精细跃迁频率定义出来的，我们接下来要做的就是造个机器来测量它。小菜一碟！铯管是这台仪器的核心，所以我们先来看看里面有什么。基本上，这就是传统铯原子束管的整体外观。

cues.en: First you have to generate a beam of neutral cesium atoms Fortunately cesium melts at a very low temperature So at about 100 C it slowly boils off and I believe it is simply formed into a beam by collimation holes Our tube has only six grams of cesium So after the cesium has all boiled off you need to change the tube at 40 K a tube This is not for the faint-hearted and also why most of the clocks you see on eBay have dead tubes
cues.zh: 首先，你得产生一束中性铯原子。幸运的是，铯的熔点非常低，所以在 100 度左右它就会慢慢沸腾蒸发。我猜它只是通过准直孔形成了一束原子。我们的管子里只有六克铯，所以等铯全部蒸发完后，你得花 4 万美元换个新管子。这可不是胆小的人能干的活儿，这也是为什么你在 eBay 上看到的时钟大多管子都坏了的原因。

cues.en: Then comes a part lifted out one of the most famous experiments in quantum physics that confirmed the existence of spin, the Stern-Galak experiment. It consists of a magnet creating an inhomogeneous field. Depending on the outer electron spin, the entire atom will be either pulled up or down. But here the weirdness of the quantum world is in full display. In quantum mechanics, there is no middle or intermediate position, not even sideways.
cues.zh: 接下来这部分摘自量子物理学中最著名的实验之一——斯特恩-革拉赫实验，该实验证实了自旋的存在。它包含一个能产生非均匀磁场的磁体。根据外层电子的自旋，整个原子会被向上或向下拉动。但这里充分展现了量子世界的诡异之处。在量子力学中，不存在中间或过渡位置，甚至连侧面都没有。

cues.en: If you measure spin along a direction, the electron has to decide from a choice of just two, either up or down, and always aligned with the direction of measurement. So the magnet splits our beam in two. Each of the beams has only atoms with the same outer electron spin state. One of the beams, now with all its electrons in the same spin, enters a microwave cavity.
cues.zh: 如果你沿某个方向测量自旋，电子只能从仅仅两个选项中做出选择——要么向上，要么向下，并且总是与测量方向保持一致。所以磁体把我们的原子束分成了两束。这两束原子中的每一个，都处于相同的外部电子自旋状态。其中一束原子，现在其所有电子的自旋都相同，进入了一个微波谐振腔。

cues.en: This is fed by a microwave frequency close to the 9.192 GHz hyperfine transition. We saw before that if an electron jumps from a quantum level to another, it emits radiation of a precise frequency. This also works in reverse. If the electron absorbs a radiation of a frequency close to the quantum level change, it will change its quantum level. In this case, we are tuned to the hyperfine transition, so we will change its spin.
cues.zh:
这由接近 9.192 GHz 超精细跃迁频率的微波频率提供。
@@
我们之前看到，如果电子从一个量子能级跃迁到另一个能级，它会发射出精确频率的辐射。
@@
这反过来也成立。
@@
如果电子吸收了频率接近量子能级变化的辐射，它的量子能级就会发生改变。
@@
在这种情况下，我们调谐到了超精细跃迁频率，因此我们会改变它的自旋。

cues.en: Moreover, if you hit it right on the head at the perfect frequency, you will flip 100% of the atoms. Note that there is an additional trick used, where there are actually two zones of interaction. This takes care of the loss of precision caused by the dispersion of velocity of the cesium atoms. The further apart the two zones, the finer the resonance. This is called the Ramsey effect, and is why the lab cesium clocks have such long tubes.
cues.zh:
此外，如果你以完美的频率准确击中它，你将翻转 100% 的原子。
@@
请注意，这里还使用了一个额外的技巧，即实际上存在两个相互作用区。
@@
这就解决了由铯原子速度色散引起的精度损失问题。
@@
两个区域相距越远，共振就越精细。
@@
这被称为拉姆齐效应，这也是实验室铯原子钟拥有如此长的管子的原因。

cues.en: But the HP engineers managed to make a very small tube, yet only lose about an order of magnitude of precision, down from 10 to minus 12 to about 10 to minus 11, which was remarkable at the time. There is one more wrinkle to this, the C field, but this is getting so complicated that this will probably be for another video. Finally, you use another stern-galak magnet to select the flipped atoms, and a detector to see how many you get.
cues.zh: 但惠普的工程师们设法制造出一个非常小的管子，精度只损失了一个数量级左右，从 10 的负 12 次方降到了 10 的负 11 次方左右，这在当时非常了不起。这里还有一个棘手的问题，就是 C 场，但这实在太复杂了，可能会留到另一期视频再讲。最后，你用另一个斯特恩-盖拉赫磁体来选出发生翻转的原子，并用探测器来看看你得到了多少原子。

cues.en: And the HP tube uses yet even more wizardry. The exit beam is directed toward a hot wire ionizer, finally getting rid of our precious outer electron. Now that our cesium is charged, we can deflect it with an electromagnet, using good old classic mechanics, this time to form a mass spectrometer. A slit selects the atoms that have the weight corresponding just to cesium, filtering out other stray ions.
cues.zh: HP 电子管还运用了更多的奇思妙想。出射光束指向一个热丝电离器，最终去掉了我们宝贵的价电子。既然我们的铯原子已经带电了，我们就可以用电磁铁来使它偏转，这次运用经典老物理，构成一个质谱仪。狭缝选出重量恰好对应铯原子的原子，过滤掉其他杂散离子。

cues.en: Then our ionized cesium atom finally hits a plate, kicks off electrons that get multiplied in an electron multiplier, and we get our current output.
cues.zh: 然后，被电离的铯原子最终撞击到极板上，击出电子，电子在电子倍增器中倍增，我们就得到了输出电流。

cues.en: Yeah, so this one has been upgraded in 1986, it's my guess. So this 1968 revised in 1986, which is why it works. And then you can see where they did the vacuum. Absolutely didn't exist until like then. So what do you get out of all of this? You get an electrical current that varies depending on how close your microwave excitation is to the hyperfine resonance.
cues.zh: 是的，所以这台设备大概是在 1986 年升级过，我猜是的。所以这是 1968 年设计、1986 年修订的版本，这就是它能工作的原因。然后你能看到他们做真空的地方。在那之前绝对是不存在的。所以这一切的最终结果是什么？你得到的是一个随微波激励与超精细共振的接近程度而变化的电流。

cues.en: Here's a plot of the signal you get out of the tube versus the excitation frequency. The several peaks are interference fringes due to the Ramsey dual cavity arrangement. The whole idea of the clock is to servo a voltage control quartz oscillator to the center of the highest peak. Here's the complete block diagram of the clock. An oven stabilized quartz oscillator generates 5 MHz. It is doubled and twice tripled to generate 90 MHz.
cues.zh: 这里是探测管输出信号随激励频率变化的曲线图。几个峰值是由 Ramsey 双腔结构产生的干涉条纹。这个时钟的核心思想是将压控石英振荡器的电压伺服控制在最高峰的中心。这是时钟的完整框图。一个经恒温槽稳定的石英振荡器产生 5 兆赫兹的频率。它经过一次倍频和两次三倍频，生成 90 兆赫兹。
